study_identification_part.si_3_author_journal_year: Pinaya et al., Human Brain Mapping, 2019
study_identification_part.si_4_title: Using deep autoencoders to identify abnormal brain structural patterns in neuropsychiatric disorders: A large-scale multi-sample study

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Deep autoencoder used as the normative model.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: We used an artificial neural network known as ' deep autoencoder ' to create a normative model using structural magnetic resonance imaging data from 1,113 healthy people.

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Cortical thickness for 68 cortical subregions and volumes of 36 neuroanatomical structures.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: These data -including cortical thickness and anatomical structural volume -have already been extracted using the Freesurfer pipeline version 5.3.0 and made available to the scientific community from the HCP. ... This procedure allowed us to calculate the cortical thickness for each of the 68 cortical subregions (34 per hemisphere) and the volume of 36 neuroanatomical structures; therefore, the total number of subregions/structures being investigating was 104.

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age and sex were included as supervised variables in the autoencoder.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: we added information about our samples (in our case, age and sex values) in the structure of the model.
